title: The Dog's Own Holiday
clue: Your dog already celebrates something every day, and nobody has ever put it on the calendar.
reveal: Watch your dog for a week, choose their gentlest, most reliable habit (the mailbox sniff, the sun spot, the bowl clink) and found a yearly holiday around it, with a name, a date, a proclamation and a very small festival.
objective: Spot a habit, name a holiday after it, hold a tiny celebration and put the date on the calendar for every year.
instructions: For a week, jot your dog's gentle, repeated habits on sticky notes: the sunny-spot sprawl, the post sniff, the stretch at the door, the first sip of water. Aim for three candidates.

Pick one that is safe and low-key. Skip chasing, barking, guarding, digging, door-darting and anything repetitive that seems driven or worried. The best holiday habits are ones your dog clearly does in a relaxed way.
Name it ('Sunbeam Day', 'Mailbox Morning') and choose a date: the day you chose, or any day that suits you. Write the name and date on a card and mark it on the calendar.

On the day, let the habit happen as it normally does and make it the star. Read a proclamation aloud in a calm voice: three lines on why this habit deserves a holiday. If your dog skips it, 'Day of Rest' is also a holiday.

Add one tiny ritual from what you have: a flat cloth or card as a 'banner' (nothing dangling), a toast with a water bowl and your mug, your dog's favorite toy laid beside the habit spot as the official gift, and the habit's moment as the official ceremony. Keep it short, quiet and at home, and let your dog leave whenever they like.
Sign the card as the founding document with the date, the name and one line of history, then set the date on the calendar for next year and the year after.
twist: Your dog already has a favorite day of the year. You give it a name, a date and a yearly repeat, and it becomes a tradition.
variations: Puppy: choose a 'first' such as the first sunny spot, keep the festival to a minute and the nap longer; habits change fast, so you may rename it next year.
Senior: pick a gentle, slow habit like the sun-spot sprawl and hold a quiet half hour with a blanket beside them.

Host's day, for your own birthday: set a folded invitation on a shelf at your height (nothing paper or cloth left with your dog), then follow your dog round the home to three places where they linger: the Welcome, the Gift (whatever they find; nothing is carried or taken) and the Toast, with fresh water for the host. The party ends when they settle.
Bigger version: every person in the household says one line at the toast, with nobody touching the dog unless invited.
completion: Counts once the holiday has a name and a date on the calendar and you have celebrated it once, even if your dog slept through it.
photoIdea: The proclamation card beside your dog's habit spot, with your dog doing the habit or simply nearby.
memoryPrompt: What is your dog's holiday called, and when will you celebrate it next?
safety: Pick calm, safe habits only; skip anything driven or worried like pacing, spinning or chasing lights.
Keep decorations flat and out of reach, nothing dangling, small or edible.
